notes: Version 1.5 synchronises the carrier-selection correction with HeisenbergStructure version 2.1. The finite S3 countermodel is no longer inventoried or cited as a separate HCO record: it is cited through the current HeisenbergStructure concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19635395. Stone-von Neumann is now typed exactly: after the Heisenberg group and a non-trivial central character are supplied, it identifies the Heisenberg/Schrodinger representation pi_c on H_c=L2(Z/qZ); the associated Weil action is distinct further symplectic data. The version 1.4 H-rank documentary correction remains in force: the parity-involution fibre reading is structural, while the conjugation identity itself is proved. Statuses are aligned with Foundation version 2.2: immediate information loss (Proposition 4.1) and projective incompleteness under A2 (Corollary 4.9) are proved; temporal order and the arrow of time (Theorem 4.4) are conditional on the unestablished acyclicity hypothesis [H-acyc] and are no longer listed as proved; irreducibility of the admissible fibre (Lemma 5.6) is conditional on a representation-theoretic dictionary; Foundation Theorem 5.7 is described as the carrier-selection obstruction it states. A section of conditional results is added. The HeisenbergStructure entry is described by its current content (Theorem 4.1 obstruction, Proposition 4.7 Schur correction, Proposition 4.8 conditional Stone-von Neumann endpoint, Corollary 5.1 conditional Robertson bound), and the separate countermodel row of the constituent-paper table is merged into it. The Born rule is not established in any sector: the earlier statement that it is proved in the SU(2) sector is withdrawn, since Q3's singlet and correlator are conditional on a supplied bipartite carrier and an unestablished diagonal 2I-invariance hypothesis. The passage from the discrete carrier to a continuous Hilbert space is no longer described as handled by the Q5a continuum limit: it is not derived; Q5a proves the zero-form Mosco limit on its canonical Fourier filtration and a normalisation no-go under its depth and weight hypotheses, and the spatial-limit operator is the unestablished hypothesis [H-L] of Q5b. The Inputs section lists the separately supplied Heisenberg group, central character and associated Weil action alongside the Born-Infeld candidate. The ENI bibliography title is synchronised with ENI version 2.7. No independent result is promoted.
